examples.knowledge_point: Determining a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
examples.problem: What is the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ whose standard matrix is $[\begin{aligned}8 & -1 \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}]$
examples.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector $[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -1 \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8x-y \\ -5x-2y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,\mathbf{T}\,$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation  $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-4y \\ -3x+y\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0\cdot x+(-4)\cdot y \\ (-3)\cdot x+1\cdot y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4y \\ -3x+y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation  $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
